source_law.title: Requirements for turning on highway (2)
source_law.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled in a business or residential district and not less than the last 300 feet traveled in any other area prior to changing the course of a vehicle. This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

legal_analysis_note: The 100-foot threshold is a statute-derived continuous traveled distance; the 300-foot other-area alternative and other maneuver/signaling modes remain separate same-law work. The business-district frontage definition must be independently reviewed on original geometry.
physical_prerequisites: Measure continuous physical indicator/hand-signal activity along actual traveled distance before course-change onset; distinguish 100-foot business/residential from 300-foot other-area branch. Confirm business or industrial building-use frontage occupies at least 300 feet in a 600-foot highway interval, via original Native context and independent source review.
legal_interpretation_limit: Weather cannot waive the distance rule; command station is not observed onset or visible flashing.
